feature:
Give the human playtest harness the R1 pre-roll dev-card window on BOTH seats, so the owner can play the Colonist-faithful ruleset against the policy.

CURRENT STATE (verified): scripts/play_vs_model.py pins RULESET_R0 at the HumanVsBotEnv.__init__ site via `kwargs.setdefault("ruleset", RULESET_R0)`. `_human_pre_roll` was DELETED by commit 6bc0cc2. Every game records `"preroll": false`. So NEITHER seat can play a dev card before rolling. That pin was correct when the bot could not pre-roll; it is now stale, because RULESET_R1 shipped and gives the bot a real pre-roll window.

TDD IS BINDING: failing test first, observed failing, before each fix. Report red-first output.

WHAT TO BUILD:

1. FLIP THE EPOCH. `kwargs.setdefault("ruleset", RULESET_R0)` -> RULESET_R1 at HumanVsBotEnv.__init__. Keep `audit_events=True` (the self-test's run_all_invariants needs the broadcast stream).

2. RESTORE THE HUMAN PRE-ROLL WINDOW. The prior implementation is recoverable at `git show 1846113:scripts/play_vs_model.py` (`_human_pre_roll`, ~line 396, and its call site at ~line 376 immediately before `game.rollDice()`). Restore it ADAPTED to R1 legality — do not restore it verbatim.

3. SEAT SYMMETRY IS THE ACCEPTANCE BAR. The human's window must offer EXACTLY the set the bot's mask offers at a pre-roll node, no more and no less:
   - INCLUDE PlayKnight, PlayYearOfPlenty, PlayMonopoly.
   - EXCLUDE PlayRoadBuilder. This is spec preroll-dev-cards-r1 D4 and it is NOT optional: `src/catan_rl/env/ruleset.py` PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES omits it, so a human Road-Builder-pre-roll would be a capability the policy structurally lacks — the exact asymmetry commit 6bc0cc2 removed, reintroduced in the other direction.
   - Respect one-dev-card-per-turn and not-bought-this-turn, both of which the engine already enforces via devCardPlayedThisTurn / updateDevCards. Do NOT re-implement those rules in the GUI; drive the same engine path.
   - A card the human plays pre-roll must consume the turn's allowance so no second card is playable post-roll.

4. THE RECORD MUST TELL THE TRUTH. `"preroll"` currently hardcodes false. It must reflect the live epoch (true under R1). A consumer reading `preroll: false` on an R1 game would silently mis-file it. Keep the key additive and keep a MISSING key meaning "predates the field".

5. DOCSTRINGS. The module docstring and the HumanVsBotEnv docstrings assert "Both seats are POST-ROLL ONLY" and explain the R0 pin at length (module docstring ~lines 47-59, the __init__ comment ~lines 331-340, and the _run_opponent_turn docstring ~lines 596-606). All of that is now false. Rewrite to state the R1 window, the Road Builder exclusion and its reason, and that both seats have identical pre-roll legality.

6. THE HEADLESS AUTO-PLAY SEAT. There is a `_no_pre_roll` suppression applied to the auto-played human seat so a headless --self-test seat could not pre-roll while the keyboard human could not. Under R1 with a real human window that suppression now CREATES an asymmetry rather than removing one. Re-evaluate it: the auto-played seat should match what a keyboard human can do. Fix or justify in a comment; do not leave the stale rationale.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT touch src/catan_rl/engine/. PINNED_ENGINE_TREE must stay 261098d190c8.
- Do NOT change env/masks.py or env/ruleset.py — the bot side is already correct and shipped. This slice is the HUMAN side plus the epoch flip.
- Do NOT add Road Builder to any pre-roll set.
- No training runs, no BC regeneration.
- `python scripts/play_vs_model.py --self-test` must pass headless at the end.

ACCEPTANCE (beyond the gate):
- A test proving the human's pre-roll option set EQUALS the bot's mask-legal pre-roll set at the same state (this is the anti-asymmetry pin and is the most important test in the slice).
- Road Builder is never offered pre-roll to the human.
- A human pre-roll play leaves no second dev card legal that turn.
- A card bought this turn is not playable pre-roll; a card bought last turn is.
- Recorded games stamp `"preroll": true` under R1.
- --self-test passes.

implSummary:
Closed the playable-and-recordable D3 stopgap: the playtest harness now runs RULESET_R1 and the human seat has a pre-roll dev-card window with legality identical to the bot's.

WHAT SHIPPED (TDD throughout — every step's test written and observed RED first; the initial run of the new `TestHumanPreRollWindowR1` class was 10 failed / 1 passed, and the two new GUI-filter pins failed with `AttributeError: 'catanGameView' object has no attribute 'dev_card_filter'` and `assert 'ROADBUILDER' == 'KNIGHT'`):

1. `scripts/play_vs_model.py` — `kwargs.setdefault("ruleset", RULESET_R0)` → `RULESET_R1` (still a setdefault, so an explicit epoch from a caller wins). `audit_events=True` untouched.
2. New `HumanVsBotEnv._pre_roll_dev_options() -> set[str]`: calls `self._compute_masks(self.opponent_player, self._opponent_env_state(roll_pending=True))` and filters the type mask through `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES`. Seat symmetry is therefore BY CONSTRUCTION — it is literally the bot's mask function at the human's own pre-roll node, per-seat epoch via `opponent_ruleset`. This matters beyond bookkeeping: `masks._set_dev_card_legality` additionally gates `PLAY_YOP` on finite-bank stock, so "the three card names" is NOT the bot's legal set in a depleted bank; a dedicated test drains the bank into the other seat's hand and pins that both seats drop YoP together.
3. New `_human_pre_roll()`, called in the GUI branch of `_run_opponent_turn` after `updateDevCards()` / the single `devCardPlayedThisTurn` reset and immediately before `rollDice()`, followed by a NEW `opp.victoryPoints >= game.maxPoints` guard mirroring `catan_env.py` — the pre-6bc0cc2 implementation lacked that guard, so a pre-roll Knight taking Largest Army used to roll on past its own win. Returns immediately when `_pre_roll_dev_options()` is empty (no dead menu on the ~95% of turns with nothing playable). Loop is PLAY DEV / ROLL DICE only and exits as soon as a card is played or the dice are clicked.
4. Restricting the picker without touching `engine/`: `engine/player.play_devCard` calls `boardView.get_dev_card_selection(self)` with ONE argument, so the restriction had to live on the view. Added an additive, optional `catanGameView.dev_card_filter` (default `None` = byte-identical to today); filtered-out cards are drawn dimmed and their clicks ignored, mirroring the existing greyed-out unsuppliable-YoP-resource precedent. Chosen over stashing `player.devCards["ROADBUILDER"] = 0`: no hand mutation, so a `sys.exit(0)` mid-window or a partial-record write can neither capture nor leak a card, and the on-screen count stays truthful. `_human_pre_roll` sets it inside a `try/finally` so `SystemExit` from the QUIT path cannot leak the restriction into the main-phase picker.
5. Deleted `_no_pre_roll` and its `base_opp.heuristic_pre_roll` rebind; the headless/auto-played seat now delegates to `super()._run_opponent_turn()` unchanged, because with a real human window suppressing the stand-in's Knight is what would create the asymmetry. A test asserts the heuristic pre-roll IS reached over a full auto-played game (was pinned at exactly 0 before), plus a source pin that `_no_pre_roll` is gone.
6. Record truthfulness: `"preroll": env.ruleset == RULESET_R1` (derived, not a literal — pinned both by source text and by an end-to-end test that plays a headless game through `play_interactive` and reads the JSONL back). Added companion key `"ckpt_ruleset"` from `eval.harness.checkpoint_ruleset` (absent stamp ⇒ `"R0"`) plus a loud console warning on mismatch — warn, never refuse, since `--self-test` legitimately runs on fresh unstamped weights.
7. Docstrings + docs sync: module docstring, `__init__` comment, `_run_opponent_turn` docstring and the `_human_interactive_main_turn` NOTE all rewritten; `CLAUDE.md`'s "Both seats are POST-ROLL ONLY" bullet replaced; terse implementation notes appended (not rewritten ratified text) to `preroll-dev-cards-r1.md` — whose closing "`play_vs_model.py` pins R0 … a separate slice" line is now explicitly marked stale — and to `playable-and-recordable.md` as a "D3 stopgap: CLOSED" section. Repo-wide grep for `preroll` / `POST-ROLL ONLY` / `_no_pre_roll` shows no surviving stale claims (`README.md`, `docs/1v1_rules.md`, `docs/io_schema.md` describe the epochs generically and were already correct).

CONSTRAINTS HELD: no `src/catan_rl/engine/` hunk, no `env/masks.py` or `env/ruleset.py` hunk, `PINNED_ENGINE_TREE` still `261098d190c8`, no pre-roll Road Builder on either seat.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN, both deliberate and flagged rather than silent:
- The plan asked for a module-level `_PRE_ROLL_TYPE_TO_CARD` dict. Building it requires importing `catan_rl.env.ruleset` / `policy.obs_schema`, which transitively imports the policy package and therefore torch — that would break the file's documented invariant that importing it never forces those imports at module load (the stated reason `_build_human_env_class` is a function). I shipped it as `@functools.cache def _pre_roll_type_to_card() -> dict[int, str]` instead, with the anti-drift assertions against `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES` / `PRE_ROLL_DEV_CARD_NAMES` inside it AND a test pinning both sets. Same drift protection, invariant preserved.
- `TestHumanSeatIsNotAI::test_play_devcard_has_only_the_two_audited_call_sites` had to change: adding the pre-roll window creates a third `play_devCard` call site. Renamed to `..._has_only_the_audited_call_sites`, updated to expect `scripts/play_vs_model.py` twice + `engine/game.py` once, and the class docstring updated. The pin's purpose (no NEW file gains a path into the `isAI` branch) is unchanged and still enforced.

ONE THING I DID NOT DO, by plan: `DEFAULT_CKPT` still points at `runs/anchors/ptr_v1_u500.pt`. The owner's spec mentions an R1-trained `ckpt_000000300`, but repointing the champion was not in the plan and `runs/` is gitignored (the file is absent from this worktree), so I left it and made the mismatch loud and recorded instead. Worth an explicit decision before the first real playtest — as it stands, `python scripts/play_vs_model.py` will print the EPOCH MISMATCH banner and log `ckpt_ruleset: "R0"` unless the checkpoint is repointed or its stamp says R1.

lenses.summary: No BLOCKERs. The slice does what the owner asked and the seat-symmetry design is genuinely structural rather than asserted: the human's menu is built from `_compute_masks(opponent_player, _opponent_env_state(roll_pending=True))`, which routes through the same per-seat `opponent_ruleset` the policy's own pre-roll mask uses, so the finite-bank YoP gate, `devCardPlayedThisTurn` and the `newDevCards` promotion apply to the human without any rule being reimplemented in the GUI. Road Builder is excluded and pinned; `engine/`, `env/masks.py` and `env/ruleset.py` are untouched (`git diff main` empty for both trees) and `PINNED_ENGINE_TREE` is still `261098d190c8`. `"preroll"` is derived from `env.ruleset`, pinned by both a source assertion and a real end-to-end JSONL test. The `_no_pre_roll` suppression is removed with an honest, non-hand-waving justification (the heuristic stand-in gets the window in kind but not in extent, and that is stated rather than glossed). The whole gate is green on real exit codes and `--self-test` passes. Any `--self-test` result recorded in the attestation must be produced with `PYTHONPATH=src` (or a worktree venv). Do NOT `pip install -e` from the worktree — that is the corruption the rule forbids. Note `scripts/play_vs_model.py` has no `sys.path` bootstrap of its own, so the guard is entirely on the invocation.

findings.issue: The drift guard for `_pre_roll_type_to_card` is two bare `assert` statements, which `python -O` strips. Under `-O` a mapping that drifted from `PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES` would silently withhold a card from the human instead of failing immediately — the opposite of the docstring's stated contract ("fails immediately instead of silently withholding it from the human").
findings.fix: Raise explicitly (`if set(mapping) != set(PRE_ROLL_DEV_TYPES): raise AssertionError(...)`), or accept it and drop the "fails immediately" claim from the docstring.

findings.issue: `checkpoint_ruleset(ckpt)` performs a second full `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` of the checkpoint that `_load_search_agent` / `_load_raw_agent` deserialized one line earlier. Harmless but it doubles the game's startup deserialize.
findings.fix: Optional: read the epoch off the already-loaded actor's config if `build_actor` exposes it, otherwise leave as-is and ignore.

findings.issue: `view.turn_banner` is set to `"YOUR TURN - play a dev card or ROLL DICE"` but never restored; only `dev_card_filter` is cleared in the `finally`. `_ViewWindow.__exit__` then repaints with the stale banner, which stays on screen until the next `__enter__` resets it to "YOUR TURN" or the driver sets "BOT IS THINKING...".
findings.fix: Restore the banner in the same `finally` that clears the filter.

findings.issue: During the pre-roll window the ROAD / SETTLE / CITY / DEV CARD / BANK TRADE / END TURN buttons are still drawn in their normal colours (`view.displayGameButtons` is unconditional) but are inert — the loop only tests `rollDice_button` and `playDevCard_button`, and `_log_human_action` produces no line for a no-op click. The dev-card PICKER got a "(greyed = not now)" hint for exactly this reason; the buttons got none. The turn banner is the only on-screen cue.
findings.fix: Either grey the inert buttons for the pre-roll pass, or accept it — the banner plus the `[PRE-ROLL]` console line is arguably enough for a single-user harness.

findings.issue: The `[PRE-ROLL]` console line prints raw engine keys (`"YEAROFPLENTY"`), while the on-screen menu labels the same card `YOP` (and `MONOPOLY`→`M`, `KNIGHT`→`K`). Minor mismatch between what is announced and what is clickable.
findings.fix: Map through the picker's own `abbreviations` / an existing display label before joining.

findings.issue: The new pre-roll call site inherits the known GUI-only defects of `engine/player.play_devCard` catalogued in the RATIFIED `human-path-conformance-fixes.md` D1: a cancelled YoP/Monopoly refunds the card and resets `devCardPlayedThisTurn` but never decrements `yopPlayed`/`monopolyPlayed` (which the policy observes), and the human's Knight runs `game.robber` BEFORE `check_largest_army`, so the two seats can be offered different Friendly-Robber-legal hexes. Not introduced here — but the pre-roll window makes the cancel loop reachable in a second place, and the pre-roll cancel loop is unbounded within a turn just like the main-turn one.
findings.fix: No action in this slice (engine/ is out of scope by spec). Flag it in the merge note so the D1 slice knows there are now two call sites to cover, and so the sequencing between the two branches is deliberate.

findings.issue: The test calls `human.updateDevCards()` and then manually sets `human.devCardPlayedThisTurn = False`. If a future change made the promotion path leave that flag set, the manual reset would hide it and the test would still pass.
findings.fix: Drop the manual reset (the flag is already False from the setup above) so the assertion depends only on the engine's promotion behaviour.

findings.issue: The `preroll` stamp is derived from the AGENT seat's epoch only (`env.ruleset == RULESET_R1`), but the HUMAN's window is gated on the OPPONENT seat's epoch: `_pre_roll_dev_options()` -> `_compute_masks(self.opponent_player, ...)` -> `catan_env.py:1300` `seat_ruleset = self.opponent_ruleset if acting_player is self.opponent_player else self.ruleset`. `HumanVsBotEnv.__init__` (play_vs_model.py:404) only `setdefault`s `ruleset`, and `CatanEnv` accepts an independent `opponent_ruleset` (catan_env.py:193). So `HumanVsBotEnv(..., opponent_ruleset=RULESET_R0)` records `preroll: true` for a game in which the human seat had NO window — the record claiming a regime the game did not run under, which is the exact property this key exists to guarantee (see its own comment at 2054-2061 and the owner spec's "the game record must never misrepresent the information regime it was played under"). Latent, not live: `play_interactive` passes no ruleset kwargs and the CLI cannot reach it. But the stamp is one `and` away from being true by construction instead of true by coincidence.
findings.fix: `"preroll": env.ruleset == RULESET_R1 and env.opponent_ruleset == RULESET_R1` (or stamp both seats' epochs). Update the adjacent comment and `test_the_record_derives_the_pre_roll_stamp_from_the_env` accordingly.

findings.issue: The DEFAULT invocation is a guaranteed epoch mismatch and the CLI never says so. `DEFAULT_CKPT = "runs/anchors/ptr_v1_u500.pt"` predates the R1 stamp, so `eval/harness.py:110` `checkpoint_ruleset` returns R0 for it, while the harness now runs R1 — every `python scripts/play_vs_model.py` with no flags seats an R0-trained policy under rules it never saw. The owner's stated goal for this slice is "so the owner can play the Colonist-faithful ruleset against the policy", and an R1-trained checkpoint exists (`ckpt_000000300`). The code handles this honestly (loud console banner at 1806-1820, `ckpt_ruleset` persisted at 2067, and the module docstring at ~88-97 explains why it warns rather than refuses and why repointing is an owner call), so this is a documented judgment call, not a spec contradiction — but the `--ckpt` help string (2218) still reads only "Bot checkpoint (default: runs/anchors/ptr_v1_u500.pt)", so the one place a user looks before running gives no hint that the default is the wrong epoch.
findings.fix: Owner decision: either bank the R1 lineage into `runs/anchors/` and repoint `DEFAULT_CKPT`, or at minimum extend the `--ckpt` help to say the default is an R0 checkpoint and that an R1 checkpoint is needed for a clean strength read under this harness.

findings.issue: The checkpoint is fully deserialized twice at startup: `_load_raw_agent`/`_load_search_agent` (line 1791) already `torch.load`s it, then `checkpoint_ruleset(ckpt)` (`eval/harness.py:106`, `weights_only=False`) loads the entire file again solely to read `config["rollout"]["ruleset"]`. On the ~361 MB champion that is a second full unpickle and a second peak-memory spike per game launch.
findings.fix: Read the epoch off the already-loaded object (the actor/policy factory has the config in hand), or hoist the epoch read to before the agent load and reuse the loaded dict. Cosmetic — a one-off startup cost.

The negative half (`'"preroll": False' not in src`) is the load-bearing part.
findings.fix: Keep the negative assertion; drop the positive source-string match, or relax it to `'"preroll": env.ruleset' in src`.

findings.issue: Undocumented search-cost consequence of the epoch flip. `forced = len(legal_actions) <= 1` short-circuits a root with one legal action; under R0 every pre-roll node WAS forced (`{ROLL_DICE}` only) and cost nothing. Under R1, as soon as the seat holds a whitelisted card the pre-roll root has >=2 actions and pays a full `--sims` search every turn. Measured in this worktree (fresh weights, seed 7, 60 bot-steps, sims=25): R0 2.7s vs R1 3.5s = 1.30x, and that ratio grows as dev cards accumulate. `--self-test` (sims=400 by default) took ~28 min end-to-end here. Not a defect — it is the price of the ruleset the owner asked for — but neither the `--self-test` help (2269) nor the `--search` help (2234) mentions that the gate's wall-clock budget just grew.
findings.fix: One line in the `--self-test` help or the module docstring noting that R1 adds a non-forced search node per turn, so search-mode wall-time is ~1.3x+ R0.
